chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from al-Hasan ibn al-Mubarak, from Zakariyya ibn Adam, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a drop of intoxicating nabidh that fell into a pot containing meat and a large amount of broth. He said: The broth should be poured out, or fed to the Ahl al-Dhimma or to dogs, and the meat should be washed and eaten. I said: And if blood fell into it? He said: The blood will be eaten by the fire, if God wills.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الذِّمَّةِ: Ahl al-Dhimma (People of the Covenant/Non-Muslims under protection)
key_terms.نَبِيذ: Nabidh (fermented drink, usually of water and dates or grapes)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when an intoxicating drop falls into food?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the purification rules for food contaminated by intoxicating nabidh, distinguishing between the liquid and solid components. The broth is discarded or given to non-Muslims or dogs, while the meat is washed and remains edible. If blood falls into the mixture, it is consumed by the fire (hellfire) on the Day of Judgment.
